verses.1:1: The pronouncement that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
verses.1:2: How long, LORD, have I cried for help, and You do not listen? I shout to You, "Violence!" and You do not save.
verses.1:3: Why do You show me iniquity and look at trouble? Devastation and violence are in front of me; there is strife, and conflict rises up.
verses.1:4: Therefore the law grows numb, and justice never comes forth; for the wicked hem in the righteous, therefore justice comes forth twisted.
verses.1:5: Look among the nations and watch; be astounded, be amazed! For I am doing a deed in your days that you would not believe if it were recounted.
verses.1:6: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, who march across the broad expanses of the earth to take possession of dwellings that are not their own.
verses.1:7: They are terrifying and fearsome; from themselves come forth their justice and their dignity.
verses.1:8: Their horses are faster than leopards and keener than evening wolves. Their horsemen gallop forward, and their horsemen arrive from afar; they fly like an eagle rushing to devour.
verses.1:9: Every one of them comes for violence; the surge of their faces is forward, and like sand they gather captives.
verses.1:10: They deride kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them. They laugh at every stronghold; they heap up earth and capture it.
verses.1:11: Then they sweep on like a wind and pass through, and incur guilt—these whose strength is their god.
verses.1:12: Are You not from of old, LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, You have appointed them for judgment, and, Rock, You have founded them for reproof.
verses.1:13: You are too pure of eyes to see evil, and You cannot look at trouble. Why do You look at the treacherous, and stay silent while a wicked man swallows up one more righteous than himself?
verses.1:14: And You have made humanity like the fish of the sea, like creeping creatures with no ruler over them.
verses.1:15: All of them he draws up with a hook; he drags them in his dragnet and gathers them in his seine. Therefore he is glad and exults.
verses.1:16: Therefore he sacrifices to his dragnet and burns incense to his seine, because by them his portion is rich and his food is choice.
verses.1:17: Will he therefore keep emptying his dragnet, and continually kill nations without pity?
verses.2:1: At my watch post I will stand and position myself on the rampart, and I will watch to see what He will speak with me, and what response I will give regarding my complaint.
verses.2:2: And the LORD answered me and said, "Write the vision and inscribe it clearly on the tablets, so that whoever reads it may run.
verses.2:3: For still the vision is for the appointed time; it hurries toward the end and will not lie. If it lingers, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.
verses.2:4: Look, his soul is puffed up, not upright in him; but the righteous one will live by his faithfulness.
verses.2:5: Indeed, wine is treacherous; an arrogant man does not settle down, who widens his appetite like Sheol; he is like death and is not satisfied; he gathers to himself all the nations and assembles to himself all the peoples.
verses.2:6: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, with satire and riddles about him, and say, 'Woe to the one who multiplies what does not belong to him—how long?—and weighs himself down with pledges!
verses.2:7: Will your creditors not suddenly rise up, and those who make you tremble wake up? And you will become plunder to them.
verses.2:8: Because you yourself have plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and violence against the land, against the city and all who live in it.
verses.2:9: Woe to the one who acquires evil gain for his house, to place his nest on high, to be rescued from the grasp of calamity!
verses.2:10: You have planned shame for your house, cutting off many peoples and sinning against your own life.
verses.2:11: For a stone from the wall will cry out, and a rafter from the timber will answer it.
verses.2:12: Woe to the one who builds a town with bloodshed and establishes a city with injustice!
verses.2:13: See, is it not from the LORD of hosts that peoples toil only for fire, and nations exhaust themselves only for emptiness?
verses.2:14: For the earth will be filled with knowing the LORD's glory, just as the waters cover over the sea.
verses.2:15: Woe to the one who makes his neighbor drink, mixing in your venom and even making them drunk, in order to look at their nakedness!
verses.2:16: You are sated with disgrace rather than glory. Drink, you too, and be exposed as uncircumcised! The cup of the LORD's right hand will pass around to you, and foul disgrace will be on your glory.
verses.2:17: For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of beasts that terrified them, because of human bloodshed and violence against the land, against the city and all who live in it.
verses.2:18: What profit is a carved image when its maker has carved it—a cast image and a teacher of falsehood? For the maker of his own creation trusts in it, making mute idols!
verses.2:19: Woe to the one who says to wood, "Wake up!" and "Arise!" to a silent stone! Will it teach? Look, it is plated with gold and silver, and no breath at all is within it.
verses.2:20: But the LORD is in His holy temple; hush before Him, all the earth!'"
verses.3:1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.
verses.3:2: LORD, I have heard the report of You; I fear. LORD, in the midst of the years revive Your deed; in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath, remember to show compassion.
verses.3:3: From Teman God came, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His majesty covered the heavens, and His praise filled the earth.
verses.3:4: And radiance was like the light; twin rays came from His hand, and there was the concealment of His power.
verses.3:5: Pestilence went ahead of Him, and plague came forth at His feet.
verses.3:6: He stood and measured out the earth; He looked and made the nations tremble. The perpetual mountains broke apart; the everlasting hills sank down. His pathways are everlasting.
verses.3:7: Under affliction I saw the tents of Cushan; the curtains of the land of Midian were trembling.
verses.3:8: Were You angry with the rivers, LORD? Was Your anger against the rivers, or Your fury against the sea, that You rode on Your horses, Your chariots of salvation?
verses.3:9: Your bow was laid completely bare; sworn were the shafts of command. Selah. With rivers You split open the earth.
verses.3:10: The mountains saw You; they writhed. A downpour of waters passed through; the deep uttered its voice; on high it raised its hands.
verses.3:11: Sun and moon stood still in their lofty dwelling at the light of Your arrows as they darted, at the radiance of the flash of Your spear.
verses.3:12: In indignation You strode across the earth; in anger You threshed the nations.
verses.3:13: You came forth for the salvation of Your people, for the salvation of Your anointed one. You shattered the head from the house of the wicked, stripping bare the foundation up to the neck. Selah.
verses.3:14: With his own shafts You pierced the head of his warriors; they stormed on to scatter me, their exultation like devouring the afflicted in secret.
verses.3:15: You trod through the sea with Your horses, the churning of many waters.
verses.3:16: I heard, and my belly trembled; at the voice my lips quivered. Decay entered into my bones, and where I stood I trembled, because I will wait quietly for the day of distress to come up against the people who attack us.
verses.3:17: Even if the fig tree does not bloom and there is no yield on the vines, though the olive's produce fails and the terraced fields yield no food, though the flock is cut off from the pen and no herd is in the stalls,
verses.3:18: yet as for me, in the LORD I will exult; I will be joyful in the God of my salvation.
verses.3:19: GOD the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like those of deer, and on my high places He causes me to tread. For the music director, with my stringed instruments.

notes.1:1: Pronouncement renders Hebrew massa, literally a lifting up or burden, used as a technical term for a weighty prophetic pronouncement or oracle.
notes.1:5: Be astounded, be amazed pairs the Hithpael and Qal imperatives of the same root (tamah) for strong emphasis. The Qal active participle po'el (doing) lacks an explicit pronoun in Hebrew and is confirmed as first-person (I am doing) by the LORD's words in v. 6.
notes.1:9: The surge of their faces is forward translates the rare hapax noun megammat (meaning uncertain: surge, thrust, set, or horde) with qadimah (forward or eastward).
notes.1:11: Sweep on like a wind renders terse Masoretic Hebrew (halaph ruah) taking ruah as an adverbial comparison; alternatively, his spirit changes.
notes.1:12: We will not die follows the Masoretic Hebrew (lo namut); rabbinic tradition lists it among the tiqqune sopherim (scribal corrections), holding that it replaced an original "You do not die."
notes.2:3: It hurries renders yapheah (from puah, breathe out, pant, or hasten); the form can also be parsed as a verbal adjective meaning testifies or witnesses (cf. Prov 14:5), pairing closely with will not lie.
notes.2:4: Puffed up renders the 3fs Pual perfect 'uppela, agreeing with feminine naphsho (his soul). By his faithfulness translates be'emunato, denoting steadfast fidelity and trust.
notes.2:5: Wine follows the Masoretic Hebrew (hayyayin), whereas the Dead Sea Pesher (1QpHab) reads wealth (hon). Settle down renders the rare verb yinveh (related to naveh, home or abode).
notes.2:16: Be exposed as uncircumcised follows the Masoretic Niphal imperative vehe'arel (root 'rl), whereas the Dead Sea Pesher and Septuagint read a metathesized form meaning and stagger. Foul disgrace renders the hapax qiqalon, an intensive form of qalon (disgrace) suggesting a wordplay on qi' (vomit).
notes.2:17: That terrified them follows the Masoretic verb yehitan (Hiphil imperfect of hatat with a 3fp suffix referring to the feminine plural beasts), whereas the Septuagint and Syriac read a 2ms suffix (will terrify you).
notes.3:1: Shigionoth transliterates the plural Hebrew musical or liturgical heading shigyonot (singular shiggayon in Ps 7:1), whose exact technical meaning is uncertain.
notes.3:9: Sworn were the shafts of command translates the notoriously terse Masoretic Hebrew shevu'ot mattot 'omer (literally oaths, rods/shafts/tribes, word) without conjectural emendation.
notes.3:13: For the salvation of Your anointed one reflects the unusual construction leyesha' 'et-meshihekha, where the noun yesha' (salvation) governs the direct object marker 'et- (or alternatively, 'et- functions as the preposition with).
notes.3:16: To come up against the people who attack us renders the terse clause la'alot le'am yegudennu; the syntax can alternatively be read with 'am as the subject (for an invading people to come up against us).
notes.3:19: GOD the Lord reflects the Masoretic order of the divine name followed by 'adonay (the reverse of the usual 'adonay plus the divine name); the divine name is pointed here with the vowels of 'elohim.
